steps.observation: You have 30 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
Conceptual tour in ≈30-sec read:

1. Tokenization & Embeddings  
   • Text (or other data) is chopped into discrete tokens.  
   • Each token is mapped to a learned vector (embedding).

2. Positional Encoding  
   • Because order matters and pure attention is order-agnostic, we add a position signal to every embedding.

3. Self-Attention (core idea)  
   • For every token, the model forms three vectors: Query, Key, Value.  
   • Similarity(Queryᵢ, Keyⱼ) = “How much should token j influence token i?”  
   • Softmax turns these similarities into weights.  
   • Weighted sum of the Value vectors gives each token a context-aware representation—so every token can “look at” every other token in the sequence in one step.

4. Multi-Head Attention  
   • Several attention sets run in parallel (“heads”), each learning different relational patterns.  
   • Their outputs are concatenated and linearly mixed.

5. Feed-Forward & Residual Paths  
   • A small position-wise neural network refines each token vector.  
   • Skip (residual) connections plus LayerNorm let information and gradients flow smoothly.

6. Stacking Layers  
   • Repeat attention + feed-forward blocks N times for deeper reasoning.

7. Output Head  
   • Final token vectors feed into a task-specific layer (e.g., softmax over vocabulary for language modeling).

Training: Adjust all weights via backpropagation to minimize a loss (e.g., next-token prediction). Result: a parallel, permutation-aware architecture that captures long-range dependencies efficiently.
